title: Partial reconstruction of conditional-entropy comparisons
target_claim: Conditional character predictability is an informative cross-corpus diagnostic when encodings and preprocessing are explicitly controlled.
reconstruction_scope: An original empirical bigram-entropy implementation on ZL3b paragraph text, one meaningful English comparison, and authored/symbol-shuffle controls; no reproduction of the paper's complete corpus or glyph-composition experiments.
value_authority: The complete actual run output and generated verification receipt are authoritative; this prose-level record is checked against them by verify_replications.py.
agreement: Voynich is more predictable than this one English prose comparison. A deliberately repetitive meaningful authored control is also highly predictable; the selected scalar alone does not classify meaningfulness.
limitations: No claim that the paper's numerical results, multilingual sample, historical texts or alternate glyph compositions have been reproduced.
ZL3b is a later corpus version; encoded EVA units and within-token, no-boundary estimator convention differ from other possible study definitions.
Equal symbol counts reduce one sampling difference but do not equalize genre, alphabet, dependence or token boundaries.
All three local normalization variants are retained; this descriptive seed was frozen after an engineering smoke run, not preregistered confirmatory research.
No independent human reproduction or external domain assessment has occurred.
next_step: Recover the original study's exact input versions, estimator conventions and encodings; independently implement a named result with a declared comparison tolerance.
